answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a grid where every agent must reach a specific vertex to certify their position. An issuer assigns spatial coordinates as a quartz anchor, and each receipt proves occupancy. A verifier acts as a jetty, reproducing the failure by re-running logs, mapping any latency discrepancy to trigger a penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach the site, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion without relay help.
